"In an absolute monarchy the monarch is bound by a written constitution" is the incorrect statement.

The other two are true statements about monarchy.

So I is the one that is not correct.

text: Which of the following statements about monarchy is correct? I. Monarchy is always an elective office contested at each election II. A monarchy is a system in which a king or queen is head of state III. Britain is an example of an absolute monarchy
explanation:
A monarchy is a system in which a king or queen is head of state — this is correct.

The other two statements are not true: "Britain is an example of an absolute monarchy" and "Monarchy is always an elective office contested at each election" both misstate the physics.

So only II is correct.

text: Which of the following statements about monarchy are correct? I. The position of monarch is normally hereditary II. In a constitutional monarchy the monarch holds unlimited power III. A constitutional monarch usually performs mainly ceremonial functions
explanation:
I and III are correct statements.

"In a constitutional monarchy the monarch holds unlimited power" is false, so II must be excluded.

The answer is I and III only.
